pr_title: Rework ResourceWatcherService to use a dedicated thread
pr_body:
Processing file updates can sometimes take a considerable amount of time due to IO, and doing this on an existing threadpool causes blockage.

At some point in the future, we should rework this to consolidate logic with `AbstractFileWatchingService` but that's a larger refactor than we have time for at the moment.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/87844

issue_context.title: ResourceWatcherService performs IO on main scheduler thread
issue_context.body:
The `ResourceWatcherService` runs all its scheduled actions on `SAME`:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/0699c9351f1439e246d408fd6538deafde4087b6/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/watcher/ResourceWatcherService.java#L97-L99

Typically these actions are `FileWatcher` instances which check a file for changes and process the file if changes are detected. We shouldn't be doing this on the main scheduler thread because IO can be quite slow. I saw some instances where some checks were taking a couple of _minutes_ each. I suggest setting up a separate scheduler for this service to avoid delaying other scheduled activity.

I'm labelling this as `:Security/Security` because we seem to use this most heavily in hot-reloading of security config.

review_comments: I don't think we need a `ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor` here, could we just use a regular `EsThreadPoolExecutor` instead? I'd rather we customized the rejection behaviour by making `ResourceMonitor` an `AbstractRunnable` and overriding its `onRejection`, although I think this would need some changes to `ThreadPool#scheduleWithFixedDelay` too.

Thanks, I'll take a look at doing that. I wasn't sure what our best practices are these days for things like this, so I'm definitely open to taking a different tack. I saw the fix, but it's still causing a bit of log spam due to the long task durations, so I think doing it on a dedicated thread (or at least not blocking a general-use threadpool about it) would be best.
Hmm what log spam are you seeing? I wouldn't expect any warnings about long-running tasks on `generic`.

I did a very silly thing; when I checked that this was still a problem... I did not filter the logs by version. If I filter out versions below 8.9.0 (where the fix you reference was released), there is no log spam. I'm going to blame it on getting too used to serverless logs and everything being a very current version all the time. I think I'm just going to close this (and the referenced issue) as I don't think there's enough of a problem remaining to justify more effort in the short term; apologies for the noise.
